name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
instructions: Support one hand and knee on a bench and set the shoulders and hips square to the floor. Let the working arm reach long while the trunk stays braced and still. Drive the elbow toward the hip, then lower to the full reach; if the torso rotates, reduce the load before shortening the row.
cues: Keep the torso square. Drive the elbow toward the hip. Reach long at the bottom.

name: Goblet Squat
instructions: Hold one dumbbell or kettlebell close to the chest with the forearms supporting it. Stand around shoulder width with the toes turned to a comfortable angle and pressure across the whole foot. Sit between the hips and stand tall; if the load pulls the chest down, use a lighter weight or a shorter depth.
cues: Keep the load close to the chest. Root the whole foot. Sit between the hips.

name: Push-up
instructions: Place the hands just outside shoulder width and set one straight line from head to heels. Lower the chest as one unit with the elbows tracking around 45 degrees from the torso. Push the floor away; if the hips and chest arrive separately, raise the hands and own the same shape.
cues: Move as one rigid line. Track the elbows behind the wrists. Push the floor away.

name: Walking Lunge
instructions: Stand tall with enough clear space to take repeatable forward steps. Step forward and lower until the back knee approaches the floor while the front foot stays planted. Drive through the front foot into the next step; if the back foot has to launch you, shorten the stride or reduce the load.
cues: Plant the whole front foot. Lower straight between the feet. Drive into the next step.

name: Farmer Carry
instructions: Stand between two dumbbells or kettlebells and take a secure grip with the feet balanced beneath you. Stand tall with long arms and the weights quiet beside the hips. Walk with short, controlled steps; if the weights swing or the stride shortens sharply, reduce the load.
cues: Stand tall between the weights. Take short, quiet steps. Keep the weights beside the hips.

name: Suitcase Carry
instructions: Stand beside one dumbbell or kettlebell and take a secure grip with the feet balanced beneath you. Stand tall with both shoulders level and the loaded arm long beside the hip. Walk a straight line with controlled steps; if the shoulder drops or the path curves, reduce the load.
cues: Keep both shoulders level. Walk a straight line. Keep the weight quiet beside the hip.

name: Lat Pulldown
instructions: Sit with the thighs secured and take a comfortable grip just outside shoulder width. Reach long overhead with the torso tall and the stack held just off its rest. Drive the elbows down until the bar reaches the upper chest, then return slowly to the full reach. If the hands tire before the back, soften the grip and reduce the load until the elbows can lead.
cues: Drive the elbows down toward the sides. Keep the chest tall and torso quiet. Reach long overhead on the return.

name: Cable Row
instructions: Sit at the cable row with the feet planted and the handle held in long arms. Reach forward from the shoulder blades while keeping the torso tall and the stack off its rest. Drive the elbows toward the back pockets, then return slowly; if the torso rocks, reduce the load before shortening the reach.
cues: Lead with the elbows. Keep the torso tall and quiet. Reach the shoulder blades forward on the return.

name: Band Pull-Apart
instructions: Stand tall with a light band held at shoulder height and a little tension already in it. Reach the hands wide until the band meets the chest, keeping the arms long and shoulders low. Return slowly; if the elbows bend or the ribs lift, use a lighter band.
cues: Reach wide with long arms. Keep the ribs quiet and shoulders low.

name: Pallof Press
instructions: Stand side-on to an anchored band and hold it at the centre of the chest. Set a stable stance, then press to long arms while the shoulders and hips stay square. Pause before returning to the chest; if the torso turns, step closer or reduce the resistance.
cues: Keep the shoulders and hips square. Press straight away from the chest. Breathe through the hold.

name: Plank
instructions: Set the forearms on the floor with the elbows beneath the shoulders. Extend the legs and squeeze the glutes to make one line from head to heels. Brace and breathe behind the tension; if the hips or lower back leave that line, end the hold.
cues: Squeeze the glutes. Hold the pelvis level. Breathe behind the brace.

name: Road Run
instructions: Begin tall with the shoulders relaxed and a small whole-body lean from the ankles. Settle into a pace you can hold, letting each foot land quietly beneath the body. Keep the stride relaxed; if breathing or form changes sharply, slow to a sustainable effort for the prescribed time.
cues: Land quietly beneath the body. Keep the shoulders and hands relaxed. Settle into a sustainable rhythm.

name: Bodyweight Squat
instructions: Stand with the feet around shoulder width and toes turned to a comfortable angle. Sit between the hips while the knees track with the toes and pressure stays across the whole foot. Stand tall; if the heels lift or the chest folds, shorten the depth and own that range.
cues: Root the whole foot. Track the knees with the toes. Stand tall through the hips.

name: Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on the back with the feet planted close enough that the fingertips can nearly reach the heels. Tuck the pelvis, drive through the feet, and lift until the hips are level between knees and shoulders. Hold the top before lowering; if the hamstrings cramp, bring the feet closer and use a shorter range.
cues: Tuck the pelvis first. Drive the floor away. Hold level hips at the top.

name: Band Row
instructions: Anchor a band securely at chest height and step back until it is lightly tensioned. Stand tall in a stable stance with both arms reaching long toward the anchor. Drive the elbows behind you, then return slowly; if the torso rocks, step closer or use a lighter band.
cues: Lead the pull with the elbows. Keep the torso tall and quiet.

name: Band External Rotation
instructions: Anchor a light band at elbow height and stand side-on, holding it with the far hand, elbow bent 90 degrees and pinned to the ribs. Rotate the forearm away from the body only as far as the elbow and torso remain still. Return slowly along the same path. Keep the load light; when the elbow floats or the body turns, the band is ahead of the rotation you are training.
cues: Pin the elbow to the ribs. Rotate through a smooth, owned range. Keep the torso still on the return.

name: Barbell Curl
instructions: Grip the bar at shoulder width with your arms hanging in their natural rest position. Curl to shoulder height with your upper arms pinned, then fight the bar down slower than it went up. Lower under control until your arms are back in the rest position — a small hip lean on the last rep is honest, a swing from rep one means the bar is too heavy.
cues: Elbows stay behind the bar. Lower slower than you lift. Settle into the rest position between reps.

name: Bench Dip
instructions: Grip the edge of a stable bench behind you, bend the knees, and keep the hips just clear of the edge. Bend the elbows straight back and lower only through the range the shoulders can hold comfortably. Press to long arms while keeping the hips close to the bench. Straighten the legs gradually only after every rep stays controlled and comfortable.
cues: Elbows point straight back. Hips graze the bench the whole way. Shoulders down, away from the ears.

name: Cable Pull-Through
instructions: Face away from a low cable with a rope between your legs, held at your hips. Walk out until the cable is taut, then push your hips back and hinge forward with a flat back. Drive your hips forward to stand tall, squeezing your glutes.
cues: Push the hips back — the arms just hold the rope. Squeeze the glutes at lockout. Flat back the whole rep.

name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
instructions: Lie chest-down on an incline bench with a dumbbell hanging from each hand. Row both dumbbells up, driving the elbows towards the ceiling, until your shoulder blades pinch. Lower to a full hang and let the weight pull the blades apart. The bench removes the cheat — whatever moves the weight here is actually your back.
cues: Chest glued to the pad the whole set. Pull with the elbows. Full hang and blade stretch at the bottom.

name: Dead Bug
instructions: Lie on your back, arms at the ceiling, knees stacked over your hips. Flatten your lower back into the floor and keep that pressure for the entire set — that pressure is the exercise. Lower one arm and the opposite leg as far as you can without the back peeling up, exhaling the whole way, then switch sides.
cues: Press the floor with your lower back — that pressure is the rep. Exhale like fogging a mirror as the limbs lower. Slow, opposite arm and leg, full control.

name: Dumbbell Flye
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with the dumbbells over the chest and the palms facing each other. Open the arms in a wide arc with one soft elbow angle until the chest reaches an owned stretch. Bring the bells back along the same arc, like hugging a barrel. Keep control through the return; the rep is won in the long arc, not by crashing the bells together at the top.
cues: Elbow angle locked the whole arc. Open to a deep working stretch, then hug the barrel back up. Lighter than you think — this movement punishes ego.

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand with a slight forward lean and the dumbbells hanging just off the thighs. Raise the arms out and slightly forward until the elbows reach shoulder height, leading with the elbows. Lower on a controlled count to keep tension through the full working arc. If the torso has to swing, reduce the load until the delts can own the path.
cues: Lead with the elbows, hands stay below them. Lean an inch forward to take the front delts out of it. Three seconds down.

name: Dumbbell Lunge
instructions: Step forward far enough that your front shin stays near vertical when you drop. Lower until the back knee hovers just off the floor, torso tall. Drive through the whole front foot to come back up — the back leg is a kickstand, not an engine.
cues: Long step, vertical shin. All the work belongs to the front leg. When you wobble, slow the descent and keep the full range.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Lunge
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand and step one foot back, lowering until the back knee hovers above the floor. Drive through the whole front foot to return to standing. The backward step lets the working foot stay planted; if the front heel lifts, shorten the step and reset the balance.
cues: The front leg does the work — the back leg just catches you. Torso tall and stacked. Place the step back soft and controlled.

name: Dumbbell Shrug
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides with your arms hanging as dead weight. With intention, pull your shoulder blades up and back behind your ears, as high as the traps will take them. Hold a full second at the top, then lower until you feel the traps stretch — the rep is the squeeze and the stretch, not the bounce in between.
cues: With intention: pull the shoulder blades up and back behind your ears. Own a full second at the top. Let the weight stretch the traps at the bottom.

name: Dumbbell Squat
instructions: Stand with dumbbells hanging at your sides and squat until your thighs are near parallel, letting the dumbbells travel straight down beside you. Drive up through the whole foot with a tall chest. Grip gives out before legs do at any serious weight — when that happens, it is time for the goblet or the bar, not straps.
cues: Let the dumbbells hang plumb at your sides. Tall chest, full foot. When grip becomes the limit, graduate to the bar.

name: Dumbbell Sumo Squat
instructions: Take a wide stance with the toes turned out and hold one dumbbell between the legs. Squat straight down between the knees while the torso stays tall. Drive through the whole foot with the knees tracking over the toes. The wider stance adds adductor demand; if the knees lose their line, narrow the stance or reduce the load.
cues: Push the knees out over the toes. Sit straight down between the heels. Tall chest, let the dumbbell hang.

name: Face Pull
instructions: Set the rope at upper-chest height, grab it thumbs-back, and step away until the stack is live. Pull the rope to the bridge of your nose while splitting your hands past your ears, letting the shoulders rotate back at the end. If you cannot hold a one-second squeeze with the shoulder blades pinned, the weight is wrong — this never becomes a heavy movement.
cues: Thumbs to the ears, elbows high. Squeeze the blades for a full beat. The weight stays humble.

name: Feet-Elevated Push-Up
instructions: Set your feet on a box or bench with your hands on the floor just wider than your shoulders. Lower your chest to the floor as one rigid line — the higher the feet, the more the shoulders take over from the chest. Press back to long arms without the hips piking or sagging. Own strict floor push-ups before you raise the feet.
cues: One rigid line, hips locked into the plank. Lead with the chest, chin packed. Earn strict floor reps before you raise the feet.

name: Hammer Curl
instructions: Hold the dumbbells at the sides with the palms facing each other and keep that neutral grip for the whole rep. Curl to shoulder height with quiet upper arms, then lower slower than you lifted. Return to the natural long-arm position; if the elbows drift or the torso rocks, reduce the load.
cues: Keep the thumbs up through the rep. Hold the elbows quietly beside the ribs. Lower slowly to the natural rest position.

name: Inverted Row
instructions: Set a bar around hip height and get under it with your body in one rigid line, heels planted. Pull your chest to the bar, leading with the elbows, and touch the same spot every rep. Lower to long arms without letting the hips sag — the plank is half the exercise. Feet further under the bar makes it easier, feet elevated makes it harder.
cues: Glutes squeezed, body one rigid plank. Pull with the elbows, chest to bar. Same touch point every rep.

name: Reverse Crunch
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent over your hips, hands flat beside you or holding something behind your head. Curl your hips off the floor, bringing the knees towards your ribs — the movement is the pelvis rolling up, not the legs swinging. Lower the hips back down slowly without letting the feet touch between reps.
cues: Roll the pelvis up towards the ribs. Lower the hips slow — that half is where the abs work. Keep the feet floating between reps.

name: Russian Twist
instructions: Sit with knees bent and heels lightly touching the floor, torso leaned back to about 45 degrees with a long spine. Rotate your ribcage side to side, eyes and chest travelling together — the hands only follow. Add weight at the chest or float the feet only once the rotation stays crisp without the lower back rounding.
cues: Turn the ribs — the arms just follow. Sit tall, long spine. Slow rotation, full control at both ends.

name: Scapular Pull-Up
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with straight arms and let your shoulders rise to your ears. Without bending your elbows, pull your shoulder blades down and back so your body lifts a few inches. Hold the top for a beat, then return to the full hang with control.
cues: Arms stay straight — this is the shoulder blades' job. Small range, done with intention. It is the first inch of every pull-up you will ever do.

name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie with one foot planted close enough that your fingertips can graze the heel, the other leg extended. Drive through the planted heel to a straight line from knee to shoulder, and hold the top until the glute, not the hamstring, owns it. If the hamstring cramps, the foot is too far out — pull it in and re-set.
cues: Hips dead level the whole rep. Heel in close for glute, further out for hamstring. Own the top before you lower.

name: Standing Dumbbell Calf Raise
instructions: Stand with the balls of the feet on a stable step, heels free, one dumbbell held while the other hand supports balance. Lower into an owned calf stretch, pause, then rise as high as the ankle allows. Add load only while the stretch and pause remain; bouncing is the giveaway that the weight has outrun the range.
cues: Pause in the bottom stretch. Rise tall over the big toe. Keep the torso quiet.

name: Triceps Pushdown
instructions: Set the elbows beside the ribs at a high cable and take a small step back so the line of pull stays live. Press to a strong lockout and hold it for a beat. Return until the forearms pass parallel; if the elbows drift forward, reduce the load and restore the triceps-led path.
cues: Elbows glued to the ribs. Squeeze the lockout for a beat. Ride the cable back up under full control.

name: Barbell Shrug
instructions: Hold a barbell in front of your thighs with straight arms, at your natural standing width. With intention, pull your shoulder blades up and back behind your ears as high as the traps will take them. Hold the top for a full second, then lower until the weight stretches the traps. The bar lets you load heavier than dumbbells — earn it with the same strict path.
cues: Up and back behind the ears, with intention. Own a full second at the top. Arms stay ropes — traps lift, hands just hold.

name: Cable Glute Kickback
instructions: Strap a low cable to one ankle, face the stack, and hold it for balance with a slight forward lean. Drive the strapped leg straight back and slightly up by squeezing the glute, then return under control. The range is shorter than people want it to be — where the lower back starts arching is where the glute stopped working.
cues: Push the heel back, squeeze at the end. Torso still, hips level. Short honest range beats a high arched kick.

name: Dumbbell Floor Press
instructions: Lie on the floor with the dumbbells over the chest, knees bent and feet planted. Lower until the upper arms meet the floor softly, pause, then press back to straight arms. The floor creates a repeatable bottom stop; if either elbow lands hard, reduce the load and own the pause.
cues: Elbows about 45 degrees, touch down soft. Pause on the floor, then drive. Wrists stacked over elbows.

name: Dumbbell Front Raise
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells in front of your thighs, palms facing back. Raise one or both arms straight ahead to shoulder height with a soft elbow, then lower on a slow count. Front delts already work in every press you do — this stays light, strict, and honest, or it is the lower back doing the raising.
cues: Lift to shoulder height, hands soft. Torso a pillar — the delts raise, the body stays. Slower down than up.

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Stand with dumbbells resting on the front of your thighs. Push your hips straight back and let the dumbbells slide down your legs, knees softly bent, until the hamstrings tell you to stop. Drive the hips forward to stand tall. The dumbbells hug your legs the whole way — daylight between them and you means the load has wandered onto your back.
cues: Hips back, dumbbells glued to the legs. Flat back, long spine. Stand up by squeezing the glutes through.

name: Floor Back Extension
instructions: Lie face-down with your arms reaching ahead. Lift your chest, arms, and legs a few inches off the floor by squeezing the glutes and upper back, hold a beat, then lower with control. Height is not the goal — a long body and a strong squeeze are. Reach LONG through fingers and toes rather than cranking upward.
cues: Reach long, then lift — length before height. Glutes squeeze first. Hold the top for a slow beat.

name: Incline Push-Up
instructions: Place your hands on a bench or sturdy surface around hip height and walk your feet back into one rigid line. Lower your chest to the edge, then press away to long arms. The higher the hands, the easier the rep — walk your hands lower over the weeks and the floor push-up arrives on its own.
cues: One rigid line, glutes switched on. Chest travels to the edge, whole body together. Lower the surface as reps get strict.

name: Preacher Curl
instructions: Set your upper arms flat on the preacher pad, chest against it, bar in an underhand grip. Curl to shoulder height, then lower slower than you lifted until your arms reach their natural long position on the pad. The pad removes every cheat you own — expect to lift less than your standing curl, and let that be information.
cues: Keep the upper arms on the pad. Lower on a three-count into the natural long position. Settle at the bottom before the next curl.

name: Sit-Up
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat, hands crossed on your chest or lightly at your temples. Curl your torso up one segment at a time until your chest meets your thighs, then roll back down the same way. The curl is the exercise — a flat-backed lever heave onto the hip flexors is a different movement wearing the same name.
cues: Peel up one vertebra at a time. Exhale on the way up. Roll down as slowly as you rose.

name: Band Good Morning
instructions: Stand on the middle of a long band and loop it across the back of your shoulders, clear of the neck. Soften the knees, brace, and push the hips back until the hamstrings load while the band stays over mid-foot. Drive the floor away and squeeze the glutes to stand; shorten the depth the moment the back starts carrying more than the hamstrings.
cues: Brace first, then send the hips back. Keep the band stacked over mid-foot. Finish tall through the glutes.

name: Cable Reverse Crunch
instructions: Attach both ankles to a low cable, lie facing away from the stack, and set the hips and knees near 90 degrees with the shoulders heavy on the floor. Tuck the pelvis first, then curl the knees toward the ribs until the tailbone lifts without throwing the legs. Set the hips down slowly while keeping cable tension; if the thighs swing but the pelvis stays put, lower the stack and earn the curl.
cues: Start with the pelvis tucked. Curl the knees toward the ribs. Set the hips down on a slow count.

name: Close-Grip Dumbbell Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with two dumbbells pressed together over the middle of the chest, wrists stacked and feet planted. Keep crushing the bells together as you lower them softly to the chest with the elbows close to the ribs. Press the pair back up as one unit; if the bells separate, the close-grip tension disappeared before the rep was finished.
cues: Crush the bells together. Stack the wrists over the elbows. Touch softly, then press as one unit.

name: One Arm Lat Pulldown
instructions: Sit or kneel square to a high cable, take one handle, and reach overhead until the shoulder blade can travel without the stack resting. Pull the elbow down toward the hip and pause when the upper arm reaches the ribs, keeping the torso quiet. Return to the full reach slowly; if the hand tires before the lat, soften the grip and let the elbow lead the next rep.
cues: Reach long at the top. Drive the elbow toward the hip. Keep the torso square and quiet.

name: Reverse Barbell Curl
instructions: Stand with a light bar in an overhand shoulder-width grip, wrists straight and elbows resting beside the ribs. Curl by closing the elbows until the forearms are near vertical, then hold the top without letting the shoulders climb. Lower to the natural long-arm rest; when the wrists fold or the shoulders rise, the load has moved ahead of the forearms.
cues: Keep the knuckles long and the wrists stacked. Close the elbows around the bar. Lower all the way under control.

name: Barbell Rear Delt Row
instructions: Take a wide overhand grip, soften the knees, and hinge until the bar hangs beneath a braced torso. Drive the elbows wide and row the bar toward the upper chest, holding long enough to feel the rear shoulders finish. Lower to long arms without rising; if the bar heads toward the stomach, the elbows have tucked and the movement has become a lat row.
cues: Brace the hinge before the pull. Drive the elbows wide. Touch the upper chest and lower under control.

name: Barbell Seated Calf Raise
instructions: Sit tall on a flat bench with the balls of both feet on a low block and settle a padded bar across the thighs just above the knees. Let the heels drop into a controlled stretch, then drive through the big-toe joints and rise as high as the ankles allow. Hold the top before lowering; if the bar starts bouncing on the thighs, the calves stopped owning the rep.
cues: Root the balls of the feet. Rise tall through the ankles. Hold the top, then lower slowly.

name: Cable Deadlifts
instructions: Set two cable handles at the lowest position, stand centred between them, and sit the hips back to take the handles with long arms. Brace, push the floor away, and extend the hips and knees together until the handles finish beside the thighs. Send the hips back before bending the knees to return; if the stack pulls the shoulders forward at the bottom, the load or range is too large.
cues: Brace before the cables leave the stack. Push the floor away through the whole foot. Send the hips back to begin the return.

name: Cable Hammer Curls - Rope Attachment
instructions: Attach a rope to a low cable, stand tall with a neutral grip, and settle the elbows beside the ribs. Close the elbows to curl the rope toward the shoulders, separating the ends slightly while the upper arms stay quiet. Return to the natural long-arm rest; if the shoulders roll forward to finish the curl, the stack is ahead of the biceps.
cues: Stand tall over quiet elbows. Curl the rope ends toward the shoulders. Reach the natural rest under control.

name: Cable Internal Rotation
instructions: Set a single cable handle around elbow height and stand side-on with the working elbow bent to 90 degrees and resting lightly against the ribs. Rotate the forearm across the torso while the upper arm stays quiet, then pause when the hand reaches the centreline. Return until the forearm points toward the cable; if the elbow floats away from the ribs, the chosen range has outrun the shoulder.
cues: Stack the wrist in front of the elbow. Rotate around a quiet upper arm. Return smoothly to the cable line.

name: Cable Rope Overhead Triceps Extension
instructions: Attach a rope to a low cable, face away in a split stance, and bring the rope overhead with the elbows beside the temples. Keep the upper arms quiet as the hands travel behind the head into a long triceps stretch. Extend the elbows and separate the rope at the top; if the torso loses its stack before the arms straighten, the cable is too heavy.
cues: Plant the split stance. Aim the elbows forward beside the temples. Reach the knuckles long at the top.

name: Cable Rope Rear-Delt Rows
instructions: Sit tall at a low cable with a rope in both hands and reach forward at shoulder height until the shoulder blades can travel. Pull the rope toward the upper chest by driving the elbows wide, separating the ends as the rear shoulders finish. Return to the full reach slowly; if the wrists beat the elbows to the finish, the arms have taken the job from the rear delts.
cues: Reach the shoulder blades forward. Drive the elbows wide toward the back wall. Separate the rope at the upper chest.

name: Calf Raises - With Bands
instructions: Stand on the middle of a long band with the handles held at shoulder height and the feet set about hip width. Root the forefeet and rise as high as the ankles allow while the hands stay quiet beside the shoulders. Pause, then lower into an owned stretch; if the hands bob to manufacture height, the calves have stopped driving the rep.
cues: Root the forefeet evenly. Rise tall through the ankles. Own the top before a slow return.

name: Kneeling Single-Arm High Pulley Row
instructions: Half-kneel facing a high cable, take one handle, and reach the working arm long while the hips and shoulders stay square. Pull the elbow down and back toward the ribs, allowing the palm to turn toward the body as the shoulder blade finishes. Return to the full reach slowly; if the hand reaches the ribs before the elbow travels, soften the grip and let the elbow lead.
cues: Reach long from a square half-kneeling base. Drive the elbow down toward the ribs. Let the shoulder blade finish the pull.

name: Tuck Crunch
instructions: Lie on your back with the hips and knees bent and the arms reaching toward the feet. Bring the ribs and pelvis toward one another, curling the shoulders up as the knees travel slightly toward the chest. Pause with the abdominals shortened, then lower both ends slowly; if the legs swing ahead of the curl, the range is longer than you own.
cues: Draw the ribs and pelvis together. Reach past the hips at the top. Lower both ends on the same slow count.

name: 3/4 Sit-Up
instructions: Set up 3/4 Sit-Up with a stable bodyweight start position and choose a load or range you can control. Brace before moving, then complete the trunk action through a range you can own without momentum. When momentum starts the rep, shorten the range and rebuild the brace.
cues: Set the pelvis before the rep. Move through a braced trunk. Own the return without momentum.

name: Alternate Hammer Curl
instructions: Set up Alternate Hammer Curl with dumbbells and choose a load or range you can control. Hold the upper arms still, curl the load through the forearms, and squeeze without lifting the shoulders. When the shoulders roll forward or the elbows travel, the load is ahead of the curl; reset lighter.
cues: Keep the upper arms quiet. Curl through the forearms. Own the lowering phase.

name: Alternating Cable Shoulder Press
instructions: Set up Alternating Cable Shoulder Press with cable machine and choose a load or range you can control. Organise the load at shoulder height, then press overhead while staying tall through the trunk. When the press path shifts or the setup lifts, the set is finished; reset before continuing.
cues: Stay tall through the torso. Stack the wrists over the elbows. Finish overhead with a quiet ribcage.

name: Alternating Floor Press
instructions: Set up Alternating Floor Press with kettlebell and choose a load or range you can control. Lower into the working range with the shoulders supported, then press through the intended line. When the press path shifts or the setup lifts, the set is finished; reset before continuing.
cues: Keep the chest open and shoulder blades set. Stack the wrists over the press line. Finish every rep through the same path.

name: Back Flyes - With Bands
instructions: Set up Back Flyes - With Bands with bands, squat rack and choose a load or range you can control. Move the arms through the intended arc with soft elbows and a shoulder position that stays set. When the torso swings, the load is stealing the rep; reset with less weight.
cues: Set the shoulder blades before moving. Lead the rep through the elbows. Lower with the same smooth path.

name: Band Good Morning (Pull Through)
instructions: Set up Band Good Morning (Pull Through) with bands and choose a load or range you can control. Soften the knees, send the hips back until the posterior chain loads, and stand by driving the hips through. When the load leaves the hips and moves into the back, reduce the range or weight before the next rep.
cues: Set the ribs down and brace first. Send the hips back into the load. Finish tall through the glutes.

name: Barbell Bench Press - Medium Grip
instructions: Set up Barbell Bench Press - Medium Grip with barbell, bench, squat rack and choose a load or range you can control. Lower into the working range with the shoulders supported, then press through the intended line. When the press path shifts or the setup lifts, the set is finished; reset before continuing.
cues: Keep the chest open and shoulder blades set. Stack the wrists over the press line. Finish every rep through the same path.

name: Barbell Incline Bench Press - Medium Grip
base_name: Barbell Incline Bench Press - Medium Grip
instructions: Set up Barbell Incline Bench Press - Medium Grip with barbell, bench, squat rack and choose a load or range you can control. Lower into the working range with the shoulders supported, then press through the intended line. When the press path shifts or the setup lifts, the set is finished; reset before continuing.
cues: Keep the chest open and shoulder blades set. Stack the wrists over the press line. Finish every rep through the same path.

name: Barbell Incline Shoulder Raise
instructions: Set up Barbell Incline Shoulder Raise with barbell, bench, squat rack and choose a load or range you can control. Move the arms through the intended arc with soft elbows and a shoulder position that stays set. When the torso swings, the load is stealing the rep; reset with less weight.
cues: Set the shoulder blades before moving. Lead the rep through the elbows. Lower with the same smooth path.

name: Barbell Shrug Behind The Back
instructions: Set up Barbell Shrug Behind The Back with barbell and choose a load or range you can control. Raise the shoulders up and back, pause behind the ears, and lower through the same path. When posture or foot strike changes, slow the pace before continuing.
cues: Stand tall before the shrug. Drive the shoulders up and back behind the ears. Own the pause before lowering.

name: Barbell Side Split Squat
instructions: Stand tall with a barbell across the back of the shoulders and the feet placed wide apart, the lead foot angled out to the side. Bend the knee and hip of the lead leg to lower toward that side, keeping the trailing leg only slightly bent. Return by extending the hip and knee of the lead leg. Complete the reps on one side, then work the other.
cues: Angle the lead foot out before you descend. Shift toward the working side. Keep the trailing leg long.

name: Bench Press - With Bands
instructions: Set up Bench Press - With Bands with bands, bench and choose a load or range you can control. Lower into the working range with the shoulders supported, then press through the intended line. When the press path shifts or the setup lifts, the set is finished; reset before continuing.
cues: Keep the chest open and shoulder blades set. Stack the wrists over the press line. Finish every rep through the same path.

name: Bent Over Barbell Row
instructions: Set up Bent Over Barbell Row with barbell and choose a load or range you can control. Reach into the start, then drive the elbows back until the upper back finishes the pull. When the hands finish before the elbows, the load is too ambitious; reset and own the pull.
cues: Set the torso before the pull. Lead with the elbows. Pause with the upper back engaged.

name: Bent Over Dumbbell Rear Delt Raise With Head On Bench
base_name: Bent Over Dumbbell Rear Delt Raise With Head On Bench
instructions: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand with an incline bench in front of you. Keeping the back in its natural arch, lean forward until the forehead rests on the bench and the arms hang straight down, palms facing each other. With a slight bend at the elbows, lift the dumbbells straight out to the side until the arms are parallel to the floor. Hold for a second, then lower along the same path.
cues: Rest the forehead on the bench throughout. Lift straight out to the side. Keep the torso still as the arms move.

cues: Roll the pelvis back to lift. Hold the knee angle throughout. Lower one segment at a time.

name: Cable Incline Pushdown
instructions: Lie back on an incline bench set in front of a high pulley, facing away from the machine, with a straight bar overhead. Take an overhand shoulder-width grip and bring the arms down so the bar sits just above the thighs. Keeping the upper arms stationary, let the bar travel back overhead in a semicircle. Pull it back down to the thighs with the lats and hold the contraction.

instructions: Sit back on an incline bench set between thirty and sixty degrees with a dumbbell in each hand. Extend the arms straight in front of you, palms facing down, dumbbells just above the thighs. Keeping the elbows locked, raise the dumbbells straight up until they are slightly above shoulder height. Squeeze for a second, then lower back to the start.
cues: Keep the elbows locked straight. Raise straight up in front. Keep the head resting on the bench.

name: Hammer Grip Incline DB Bench Press
base_name: Hammer Grip Incline DB Bench Press
instructions: Lie back on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand resting on the thighs, palms facing each other. Use the thighs to help clean the dumbbells up one at a time until you hold them at shoulder width. Keeping the neutral grip, set the upper arms in line with the shoulders and the elbows bent to about ninety degrees. Lower the weights to the sides under full control, then press back up and hold the lockout for a second.
cues: Keep the palms facing each other. Keep the elbows in line with the shoulders. Lower twice as slowly as you press.

name: Hip Extension with Bands

Soften the knees, send the hips back until the posterior chain loads, and stand by driving the hips through. When the load leaves the hips and moves into the back, reduce the range or weight before the next rep.
cues: Set the ribs down and brace first. Send the hips back into the load. Finish tall through the glutes.

name: Rope Crunch
instructions: Set up Rope Crunch with cable machine and choose a load or range you can control. Brace before moving, then complete the trunk action through a range you can own without momentum. When momentum starts the rep, shorten the range and rebuild the brace.
cues: Set the pelvis before the rep. Move through a braced trunk. Own the return without momentum.

name: Rope Straight-Arm Pulldown
instructions: Stand facing a high pulley with a rope, feet staggered, arms extended up and in front of you and a slight hinge at the hips. Keeping the elbows straight, sweep the rope down in an arc until the hands reach the thighs. Return overhead under control; when the elbows start to bend, reduce the load.
cues: Keep the elbows straight the whole rep. Move from the shoulders. Feel the lats finish the arc.

name: Seated Cable Rows
instructions: Set up Seated Cable Rows with cable machine and choose a load or range you can control. Reach into the start, then drive the elbows back until the upper back finishes the pull. When the hands finish before the elbows, the load is too ambitious; reset and own the pull.
cues: Set the torso before the pull. Lead with the elbows. Pause with the upper back engaged.

name: Seated Cable Shoulder Press
instructions: Set up Seated Cable Shoulder Press with cable machine and choose a load or range you can control. Organise the load at shoulder height, then press overhead while staying tall through the trunk. When the press path shifts or the setup lifts, the set is finished; reset before continuing.
cues: Stay tall through the torso. Stack the wrists over the elbows. Finish overhead with a quiet ribcage.

name: Seated Dumbbell Palms-Down Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit on the edge of a flat bench with the forearms resting on the thighs, palms facing down and the wrists just past the knees. Let the wrists drop, then lift the backs of the hands as far as the range allows without the elbows moving. Lower slowly; when the elbows lift to help, reduce the load.
cues: Keep the forearms flat and still. Lift the backs of the hands. Own the full return.

name: Seated Dumbbell Palms-Up Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit on the edge of a flat bench with the forearms resting on the thighs, palms facing up and the wrists just past the knees. Let the wrists open under the load, then curl the palms up as far as the range allows without the elbows moving. Lower slowly into the stretch; when the elbows lift to help, reduce the load.
cues: Keep the forearms flat and still. Curl the palms toward the forearms. Own the full return.

name: Seated Dumbbell Press
instructions: Sit on a bench with a back support, a dumbbell in each hand cleaned from the thighs to shoulder height, palms turned to face forward. Brace, then press both dumbbells overhead until they meet at the top. Pause, then lower to the shoulders under control; when the back arches off the bench, reduce the load.
cues: Keep the back on the bench. Stack the wrists over the elbows. Finish overhead with a quiet ribcage.

name: Seated Side Lateral Raise
instructions: Sit at the end of a flat bench with the feet firmly on the floor and a dumbbell in each hand hanging by your sides, palms facing in. Keeping the torso still, lift the dumbbells out to the side with a slight bend at the elbow, hands tilted slightly forward as if pouring water. Continue until the arms are parallel to the floor and pause for a second. Lower back down slowly to the start.
cues: Lift out to shoulder level. Tilt the hands as if pouring water. Keep the torso quiet throughout.

name: Shotgun Row
instructions: Set up Shotgun Row with cable machine and choose a load or range you can control. Reach into the start, then drive the elbows back until the upper back finishes the pull. When the hands finish before the elbows, the load is too ambitious; reset and own the pull.
cues: Set the torso before the pull. Lead with the elbows. Pause with the upper back engaged.

name: Shoulder Press - With Bands
instructions: Set up Shoulder Press - With Bands with bands and choose a load or range you can control. Organise the load at shoulder height, then press overhead while staying tall through the trunk. When the press path shifts or the setup lifts, the set is finished; reset before continuing.
cues: Stay tall through the torso. Stack the wrists over the elbows. Finish overhead with a quiet ribcage.

name: Spider Curl
instructions: Set up Spider Curl with barbell, bench and choose a load or range you can control. Hold the upper arms still, curl the load through the forearms, and squeeze without lifting the shoulders. When the shoulders roll forward or the elbows travel, the load is ahead of the curl; reset lighter.
cues: Keep the upper arms quiet. Curl through the forearms. Own the lowering phase.

name: Standing Biceps Cable Curl
instructions: Set up Standing Biceps Cable Curl with cable machine and choose a load or range you can control. Hold the upper arms still, curl the load through the forearms, and squeeze without lifting the shoulders. When the shoulders roll forward or the elbows travel, the load is ahead of the curl; reset lighter.
cues: Keep the upper arms quiet. Curl through the forearms. Own the lowering phase.

name: Standing Cable Chest Press
instructions: Set up Standing Cable Chest Press with cable machine and choose a load or range you can control. Lower into the working range with the shoulders supported, then press through the intended line. When the press path shifts or the setup lifts, the set is finished; reset before continuing.
cues: Keep the chest open and shoulder blades set. Stack the wrists over the press line. Finish every rep through the same path.

name: Standing Dumbbell Press
instructions: Stand with the feet shoulder width apart and raise the dumbbells to head height, elbows out at about ninety degrees. Brace, then press both dumbbells overhead until the arms finish straight, without leg drive or leaning back. Pause, then lower to the start under control.
cues: Stay tall through the torso. Stack the wrists over the elbows. Finish overhead with a quiet ribcage.

name: Standing Dumbbell Triceps Extension
instructions: Set up Standing Dumbbell Triceps Extension with dumbbells and choose a load or range you can control. Keep the elbows organised while the forearms extend, then return into a controlled stretch. When the elbows chase the load, the extension has lost its line; shorten the range or load.
cues: Aim the elbows through one steady line. Extend through the forearms. Control the return into the stretch.

name: Standing Overhead Barbell Triceps Extension
instructions: Set up Standing Overhead Barbell Triceps Extension with barbell and choose a load or range you can control. Keep the elbows organised while the forearms extend, then return into a controlled stretch. When the elbows chase the load, the extension has lost its line; shorten the range or load.
cues: Aim the elbows through one steady line. Extend through the forearms. Control the return into the stretch.

name: Standing Palm-In One-Arm Dumbbell Press
instructions: Stand with the feet shoulder width apart, one dumbbell at shoulder height in a neutral grip, palm facing in. Hold the incline bench with the free hand to keep your balance throughout the set. Press until the arm is fully extended overhead, then lower until the elbow returns to about ninety degrees. Finish all reps on one side, then switch arms.
cues: Keep the palm facing in throughout. Let the free hand steady you on the bench. Keep the forearm stacked under the bell.

name: Standing Rope Crunch
instructions: Set up Standing Rope Crunch with cable machine and choose a load or range you can control. Brace before moving, then complete the trunk action through a range you can own without momentum. When momentum starts the rep, shorten the range and rebuild the brace.
cues: Set the pelvis before the rep. Move through a braced trunk. Own the return without momentum.

name: Step-up with Knee Raise
instructions: Stand facing a box or bench of a height you can control, feet together. Step up by placing one whole foot on the top and extending the hip and knee to stand tall. As you stand, drive the opposite knee up as high as you can. Reverse the motion to step down, then repeat on the other leg.
cues: Drive through the whole stepping foot. Stand tall before the knee comes up. Lower under control on every rep.

name: Stiff Leg Barbell Good Morning
instructions: Set up Stiff Leg Barbell Good Morning with barbell, squat rack and choose a load or range you can control. Soften the knees, send the hips back until the posterior chain loads, and stand by driving the hips through. When the load leaves the hips and moves into the back, reduce the range or weight before the next rep.
cues: Set the ribs down and brace first. Send the hips back into the load. Finish tall through the glutes.

name: Trail Running/Walking
instructions: Set up Trail Running/Walking with a stable bodyweight start position and choose a load or range you can control. Move at a sustainable pace while keeping each stride and change of direction deliberate. When posture or foot strike changes, slow the pace before continuing.
cues: Set a repeatable starting position. Keep every stride smooth and quiet. Finish with the same posture you started with.

name: Triceps Pushdown - Rope Attachment
instructions: Set up Triceps Pushdown - Rope Attachment with cable machine and choose a load or range you can control. Keep the elbows organised while the forearms extend, then return into a controlled stretch. When the elbows chase the load, the extension has lost its line; shorten the range or load.
cues: Aim the elbows through one steady line. Extend through the forearms. Control the return into the stretch.

name: Underhand Cable Pulldowns
instructions: Set up Underhand Cable Pulldowns with cable machine and choose a load or range you can control. Set the shoulders before bending the elbows, then pull through the full available range. When the hands finish before the elbows, the load is too ambitious; reset and own the pull.
cues: Set the shoulders before bending the elbows. Pull through the elbows, not the hands. Reach long under control.

name: Upright Barbell Row
instructions: Set up Upright Barbell Row with barbell and choose a load or range you can control. Set the shoulders before bending the elbows, then pull through the full available range. When the hands finish before the elbows, the load is too ambitious; reset and own the pull.
cues: Set the shoulders before bending the elbows. Pull through the elbows, not the hands. Reach long under control.

instructions: Set up Upright Row - With Bands with bands and choose a load or range you can control. Set the shoulders before bending the elbows, then pull through the full available range. When the hands finish before the elbows, the load is too ambitious; reset and own the pull.
cues: Set the shoulders before bending the elbows. Pull through the elbows, not the hands. Reach long under control.

name: V-Bar Pullup

cues: Set the shoulders before bending the elbows. Pull through the elbows, not the hands. Reach long under control.
